patch.description: Rockefeller Institute’s June 2026 report says Lysander adopted a six-month data-center moratorium on May 7 amid opposition to a reported 300 MW Ranalli proposal. The town’s Local Law 4 pauses new applications; this does not support the pin’s $2B, 400-acre or October 2027 opening claims.

references.title: Updates on the Cloud: More Moratoriums on Data Centers
Town of Lysander — Local Law No. 4 of 2026

patch.longFormSummary:
• The report describes a roughly 120-acre proposal; other marketing reports 124 acres. Neither supports 400 acres. Reported MW is planned demand, not confirmed IT or an energized facility.
  • The proposed six-month law controls new applications and suspends relevant approval time periods. Exact effective date, exemptions, later extensions and a current site-specific application need town-record verification.
  • Timeline: May 7, 2026 is the reported adoption event, replacing unsupported October 2027 COD. The primary law text and Institute reporting support the pause; no final operating schedule is established.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Reported town adoption date in Rockefeller Institute; event is moratorium adoption, not opening.

power.note: Reported proposed demand, not verified IT allocation or operating capacity.

gaps: Obtain adopted town minutes/effective date, any extension or exemption, exact applicant/site, 120-vs-124-acre boundary, utility agreement and COD. Original Eagle News page restricted; no final permit asserted.

patch.description: BrightNight’s community page describes a 400 MW solar-and-battery project across 3,100 acres in Brantley and Wayne Counties. EIA lists separate 900 MW and 1,200 MW solar configurations plus 400 MW battery for the named plant; those cannot safely be added or substituted for the operator’s published scope.

patch.title: Steward Creek: TerraForm Acquires 1.56 GW Development; Phases Target 2029–2030
patch.description: TerraForm’s February 2026 announcement confirms acquisition of Steward Creek from Hexagon, describing a 1.56 GW development and a 600 MW interconnection agreement. Phase 1 targets 2029 operation, followed by Phase 2 in 2030. The $1.4B budget is not published.
